title: Tensor train compression and truncation error

items.title: Finite tensor arrays and the Frobenius inner product
items.statement:
Fix a field $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, an integer $d\ge2$, and positive integers $n_1,\ldots,n_d$. A finite order-$d$ tensor of shape $(n_1,\ldots,n_d)$ is an array $A=(A_{i_1,\ldots,i_d})$ indexed by $1\le i_k\le n_k$. Its Frobenius inner product and norm are
$$ \langle A,B\rangle_F=\sum_{i_1=1}^{n_1}\cdots\sum_{i_d=1}^{n_d}\overline{A_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}}B_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}, \qquad \|A\|_F=\sqrt{\langle A,A\rangle_F}. $$
For a matrix, rank means the dimension of its column image and the Frobenius inner product is the same entrywise formula. The adjoint $M^*$ is conjugate transpose (transpose over $\mathbb R$).

For $1\le k\le d$, the mode-$k$ unfolding $A_{(k)}$ has $n_k$ rows and $\prod_{j\ne k}n_j$ columns. Its row index is $i_k$ and its column index is the remaining tuple in increasing mode order, lexicographically ordered. Its entry at that row and column is the corresponding entry of $A$. For $1\le k<d$, the cut-$k$ unfolding $A^{\langle k\rangle}$ has row tuple $(i_1,\ldots,i_k)$ and column tuple $(i_{k+1},\ldots,i_d)$, each lexicographically ordered. These conventions fix all reshapes used below.

references.title: Ivan V. Oseledets, Tensor-Train Decomposition, SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 33(5) (2011), §§2–4
Tamara G. Kolda and Brett W. Bader, Tensor Decompositions and Applications, SIAM Review 51(3) (2009), §§2–4
Lieven De Lathauwer, Bart De Moor, and Joos Vandewalle, A Multilinear Singular Value Decomposition, SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 21(4) (2000), §§2–3

items.title: Tensor unfoldings preserve the Frobenius inner product
items.statement: For tensors $A,B$ of the same finite shape, every mode unfolding and every cut unfolding preserves the Frobenius inner product and norm.

references.title: Tamara G. Kolda and Brett W. Bader, Tensor Decompositions and Applications, SIAM Review 51(3) (2009), §2.4
Lieven De Lathauwer, Bart De Moor, and Joos Vandewalle, A Multilinear Singular Value Decomposition, SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 21(4) (2000), §2

items.title: Tucker format, multilinear rank, and mode products
items.statement:
For a tensor $A\in\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$, its multilinear rank is
$$ \operatorname{mlrank}(A)=\bigl(\operatorname{rank}A_{(1)},\ldots,\operatorname{rank}A_{(d)}\bigr). $$
If $U\in\mathbb F^{m\times n_k}$, the mode-$k$ product $A\times_k U$ is the tensor with mode-$k$ size $m$ and entries
$$ (A\times_k U)_{i_1,\ldots,i_{k-1},j,i_{k+1},\ldots,i_d} =\sum_{i_k=1}^{n_k}A_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}U_{j,i_k}. $$
The product is bilinear in the entries; no conjugation is used in this tensor contraction.

A Tucker representation with mode ranks bounded by $r=(r_1,\ldots,r_d)$ is a factorization
$$ A=G\times_1 U_1\times_2\cdots\times_d U_d, $$
where $U_k\in\mathbb F^{n_k\times r_k}$ and $G\in\mathbb F^{r_1\times\cdots\times r_d}$. Separately, write
$$ \mathcal T_r=\{B\in\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}:\operatorname{rank}B_{(k)}\le r_k\text{ for each }k\} $$
for the multilinear-rank-bounded set used in approximation statements.

references.title: Tamara G. Kolda and Brett W. Bader, Tensor Decompositions and Applications, SIAM Review 51(3) (2009), §§2.4, 4
Lieven De Lathauwer, Bart De Moor, and Joos Vandewalle, A Multilinear Singular Value Decomposition, SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 21(4) (2000), §§2–3
ACM 270-1, Complete Lecture Notes, Caltech, Spring 2019, Lecture 14, §3

items.title: Tensor train cores, bond ranks, and canonical gauges
items.statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$ with $d\ge2$. A tensor-train (TT) representation consists of integers $r_0=r_d=1$, internal bond sizes $r_1,\ldots,r_{d-1}\in\mathbb N_0$, and cores
$$ G_k\in\mathbb F^{r_{k-1}\times n_k\times r_k}\quad(1\le k\le d) $$
such that
$$ A_{i_1,\ldots,i_d} =\sum_{\alpha_1=1}^{r_1}\cdots\sum_{\alpha_{d-1}=1}^{r_{d-1}} G_1(1,i_1,\alpha_1)G_2(\alpha_1,i_2,\alpha_2)\cdots G_d(\alpha_{d-1},i_d,1). $$
An empty bond index set gives an empty sum, hence the zero tensor; in particular, all internal bond sizes zero represent zero. A bond size $r_k$ is the storage dimension contracted between cores $k$ and $k+1$. The cut-$k$ unfolding groups modes $1,\ldots,k$ against $k+1,\ldots,d$ as fixed in [[def-finite-tensor-arrays-and-frobenius-inner-product]].

For an internal bond $k$, an invertible matrix $S\in\mathbb F^{r_k\times r_k}$ gives a gauge transformation by replacing the two adjacent cores with
$$ \widetilde G_k(\alpha,i,\beta)=\sum_{\gamma=1}^{r_k}G_k(\alpha,i,\gamma)S_{\gamma\beta}, \qquad \widetilde G_{k+1}(\beta,j,\eta)=\sum_{\gamma=1}^{r_k}(S^{-1})_{\beta\gamma}G_{k+1}(\gamma,j,\eta). $$
Their contraction is unchanged because $\sum_\beta S_{\gamma\beta}(S^{-1})_{\beta\gamma'}=\delta_{\gamma,\gamma'}$.

The left matricization of core $G_k$ has row index $(\alpha_{k-1},i_k)$ and column index $\alpha_k$. The core is left-isometric if this matrix $L_k$ satisfies $L_k^*L_k=I_{r_k}$. The right matricization has row index $\alpha_{k-1}$ and column index $(i_k,\alpha_k)$; the core is right-isometric if its matrix $R_k$ satisfies $R_kR_k^*=I_{r_{k-1}}$. A TT is in mixed canonical gauge about core $\ell$ when cores $k<\ell$ are left-isometric and cores $k>\ell$ are right-isometric.

references.title: Ivan V. Oseledets, Tensor-Train Decomposition, SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 33(5) (2011), §§2–4
Mi-Song Dupuy, Tensor trains for high-dimensional problems, full lecture notes, Chapter 1, §§1.2.1–1.2.5 (2026)

items.title: Canonical polyadic rank
items.statement:
For $A\in\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$, its canonical polyadic rank (CP rank) is the least integer $R\ge0$ for which
$$ A=\sum_{q=1}^{R}a_q^{(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes a_q^{(d)},\qquad a_q^{(k)}\in\mathbb F^{n_k}. $$
The empty sum is zero, so the zero tensor has CP rank $0$. The coordinate expansion
$$ A=\sum_{i_1=1}^{n_1}\cdots\sum_{i_d=1}^{n_d} A_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}\,e_{i_1}^{(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_d}^{(d)} $$
shows that the set of admissible finite integers $R$ is nonempty. The well-ordering of $\mathbb N_0$ therefore makes the least such $R$ well-defined.

references.title: Tamara G. Kolda and Brett W. Bader, Tensor Decompositions and Applications, SIAM Review 51(3) (2009), §3
ACM 270-1, Complete Lecture Notes, Caltech, Spring 2019, Lecture 13, §4.2

items.title: Best rank-k matrix approximation in Frobenius norm
items.statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$, where $m,n\ge1$, have a singular value decomposition
$$ A=\sum_{j=1}^{q}\sigma_j u_jv_j^*,\qquad \sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_q>0, $$
where $q=\operatorname{rank}(A)$. For an integer $k\ge0$, put
$$ A_k=\sum_{j=1}^{\min(k,q)}\sigma_j u_jv_j^*, \qquad \delta_k^2=\sum_{j=k+1}^{q}\sigma_j^2 $$
with an empty sum equal to zero. Then $\operatorname{rank}(A_k)\le k$, $\|A-A_k\|_F=\delta_k$, and every matrix $B$ with $\operatorname{rank}(B)\le k$ satisfies $\|A-B\|_F\ge\delta_k$.

references.title: Mi-Song Dupuy, Tensor trains for high-dimensional problems, full lecture notes, Chapter 1, §1.1.1, Theorem 1.1.2 (2026)

items.title: Full-column-rank matrix least squares has a unique minimizer
items.statement:
Let $p,r,s\ge1$, let $M\in\mathbb F^{p\times r}$ have full column rank, and let $Y\in\mathbb F^{p\times s}$. Among all $W\in\mathbb F^{r\times s}$, the function $W\mapsto\|Y-MW\|_F$ has the unique minimizer
$$ W_*=(M^*M)^{-1}M^*Y. $$

references.title: ACM 270-1, Complete Lecture Notes, Caltech, Spring 2019, Lecture 13, §4.3
Tamara G. Kolda and Brett W. Bader, Tensor Decompositions and Applications, SIAM Review 51(3) (2009), §3.4

items.title: Sequential tensor-train SVD
items.statement:
Work in exact arithmetic over $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. The input is a tensor $A\in\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$ with $d\ge2$, and exactly one of:

- rank caps $c_1,\ldots,c_{d-1}\in\mathbb N_0$; or
- absolute tail tolerances $\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_{d-1}\in[0,\infty)$.

At cut $k$, flatten the current remainder with rows $(\alpha_{k-1},i_k)$ and columns $(i_{k+1},\ldots,i_d)$, where $\alpha_0=1$, and compute an exact compact SVD $M_k=U_k\Sigma_kV_k^*$. Its positive singular values are ordered decreasingly as $\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_s$. Under rank caps choose $q_k=\min(c_k,s)$. Under tolerances choose the least $q_k\in\{0,\ldots,s\}$ for which $\sum_{j>q_k}\sigma_j^2\le\tau_k^2$. This set is nonempty because $q_k=s$ gives tail zero. Record the discarded tail
$$ \delta_k=\left(\sum_{j>q_k}\sigma_j^2\right)^{1/2}. $$

Reshape the first $q_k$ columns of $U_k$ into core $G_k$ and reshape $\Sigma_{k,1:q_k}V_{k,1:q_k}^*$ as the next remainder. After cut $d-1$, reshape the remaining matrix as $G_d$. If $q_k=0$, the remainder has zero row dimension; all later ranks and tails are set to zero and the remaining cores are the corresponding empty zero arrays. Thus the zero tensor has all internal ranks zero, a cap zero returns the zero tensor, and a tolerance large enough to select $q_k=0$ does the same. The output is the TT core list and the cut tails $(\delta_k)$. Any SVD tie at a retained cutoff may be resolved by any orthonormal choice within the tied singular subspace.

references.title: Ivan V. Oseledets, Tensor-Train Decomposition, SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 33(5) (2011), §2
Mi-Song Dupuy, Tensor trains for high-dimensional problems, full lecture notes, Chapter 1, §§1.2.1, 1.2.4 (2026)

items.title: Tensor-train rounding
items.statement:
Work in exact arithmetic over $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. The input is a valid TT core list for a tensor of order $d\ge2$ and exactly one of rank caps $c_1,\ldots,c_{d-1}\in\mathbb N_0$ or absolute tail tolerances $\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_{d-1}\in[0,\infty)$.

1. **Left orthogonalize without truncation.** For $k=1,\ldots,d-1$, reshape core $G_k$ into a matrix with rows $(\alpha_{k-1},i_k)$ and columns $\alpha_k$. Compute an exact compact SVD $M=U\Sigma V^*$, replace $G_k$ by the reshape of $U$, and absorb $\Sigma V^*$ into the next core along their common bond. Omitting zero singular directions is exact. The resulting cores $G_1,\ldots,G_{d-1}$ are left-isometric.

2. **Truncate from right to left.** For $k=d,d-1,\ldots,2$, reshape the current $G_k$ into a matrix $M_k$ with rows $\alpha_{k-1}$ and columns $(i_k,\alpha_k)$, and compute an exact compact SVD $M_k=U_k\Sigma_kV_k^*$. If its positive singular values are $\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_s>0$, choose $q_{k-1}=\min(c_{k-1},s)$ for rank caps, or the least $q_{k-1}\in\{0,\ldots,s\}$ with $\sum_{j>q_{k-1}}\sigma_j^2\le\tau_{k-1}^2$ for tolerances. Record $\delta_{k-1}=(\sum_{j>q_{k-1}}\sigma_j^2)^{1/2}$. Replace $G_k$ by the reshape of the first $q_{k-1}$ rows of $V_k^*$ and absorb $U_{k,1:q}\Sigma_{k,1:q}$ into the previous core.

If $q_{k-1}=0$, the represented tensor becomes zero; set all remaining internal ranks to zero and their unperformed tails to zero. If the input represents zero, return the all-zero-rank representation and zero tails immediately. The output is the rounded core list and all recorded cut tails. No finite-precision error guarantee is part of this exact-arithmetic procedure.

references.title: Ivan V. Oseledets, Tensor-Train Decomposition, SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 33(5) (2011), §3
Mi-Song Dupuy, Tensor trains for high-dimensional problems, full lecture notes, Chapter 1, §1.2.4, Algorithm 1.3; §1.2.5 (2026)

items.title: Tensor-train storage and inner-product costs
items.statement:
If a TT representation has mode sizes $n_k$ and bond sizes $r_0=r_d=1,r_1,\ldots,r_{d-1}$, its core storage is exactly
$$ \sum_{k=1}^d n_kr_{k-1}r_k $$
field entries. If $A$ and $B$ have TT cores of bond sizes $r_k$ and $s_k$, respectively, their Frobenius inner product can be computed with
$$ O\!\left(\sum_{k=1}^d n_kr_{k-1}s_{k-1}r_ks_k\right) $$
scalar arithmetic operations and $O(\max_k r_ks_k)$ additional workspace entries.

references.title: Ivan V. Oseledets, Tensor-Train Decomposition, SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 33(5) (2011), §4.2
Mi-Song Dupuy, Tensor trains for high-dimensional problems, full lecture notes, Chapter 1, §1.2 (2026)

items.title: Higher-order SVD truncation
items.statement:
Work in exact arithmetic over $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Given $A\in\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$ and integer rank caps $0\le r_k\le n_k$, compute an exact SVD of each mode unfolding $A_{(k)}$. Let $U_k$ consist of the first $q_k=\min(r_k,\operatorname{rank}A_{(k)})$ left singular vectors, with any orthonormal choice at a tied cutoff. Define $P_k=U_kU_k^*$, the orthogonal projection onto their span; for $q_k=0$, set $P_k=0$.

For auxiliary cores and intermediate arrays in this procedure, allow mode sizes $m_k\ge0$: an array of shape $(m_1,\ldots,m_d)$ is a function from $\prod_{k=1}^d\{1,\ldots,m_k\}$ to $\mathbb F$. If a mode size is zero, this is the unique empty array. Extend the mode-product entry formula of [[def-tucker-multilinear-rank-and-mode-products]] to these arrays, taking every empty sum to be zero.

Return the factors $U_k\in\mathbb F^{n_k\times q_k}$, the core $G=A\times_1U_1^*\times_2\cdots\times_dU_d^*$ of shape $(q_1,\ldots,q_d)$, and reconstruction
$$ \widehat A=G\times_1U_1\times_2\cdots\times_dU_d =A\times_1P_1\times_2\cdots\times_dP_d. $$
If any $q_k=0$, return the corresponding $n_k\times0$ empty factor, the empty core of the stated shape, and the zero reconstruction of the original physical shape, using the same formulas and empty-sum convention. The algorithm makes no finite-precision claim.

references.title: Lieven De Lathauwer, Bart De Moor, and Joos Vandewalle, A Multilinear Singular Value Decomposition, SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 21(4) (2000), §§3, 5
Tamara G. Kolda and Brett W. Bader, Tensor Decompositions and Applications, SIAM Review 51(3) (2009), §4.2

items.title: Budgeted CP alternating least squares
items.statement:
Work in exact arithmetic over $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Inputs are a tensor $A\in\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$, a proposed CP component count $R\in\mathbb N_0$, initial factor matrices $F_k\in\mathbb F^{n_k\times R}$, and a finite sweep budget $N_{\max}\in\mathbb N_0$. The objective is
$$ \Phi(F_1,\ldots,F_d)=\left\|A-\sum_{j=1}^{R}F_1(:,j)\otimes\cdots\otimes F_d(:,j)\right\|_F^2. $$
On every exit, return the tuple $(F_1,\ldots,F_d,\widehat A,\text{status})$, where
$$ \widehat A=\sum_{j=1}^{R}F_1(:,j)\otimes\cdots\otimes F_d(:,j) $$
is evaluated from the factor matrices as they stand at that exit. If $R=0$, return the empty factor matrices, the zero model, and status “rank-zero-model” immediately. If $N_{\max}=0$, return the current factors and model with status “budget-exhausted”. Otherwise, for each of at most $N_{\max}$ sweeps, visit modes $k=1,\ldots,d$ in that order. With the other factors fixed, form $Z_k$ whose rows are indexed by all tuples $(i_\ell)_{\ell\ne k}$ and whose column $j$ is
$$ (Z_k)_{(i_\ell)_{\ell\ne k},j}=\prod_{\ell\ne k}(F_\ell)_{i_\ell,j}. $$
The mode-$k$ unfolding model is $A_{(k)}\approx XZ_k^{\mathsf T}$. If $Z_k$ is not full column rank, halt and return the current factors and model with status “rank-deficient-design”; no factor has changed at this block. If it has full column rank, solve the equivalent adjoint problem
$$ \min_{Y\in\mathbb F^{R\times n_k}}\|A_{(k)}^*-\overline{Z_k}Y\|_F $$
and replace $F_k$ by $Y^*$. The matrix $\overline{Z_k}$ has full column rank, so the minimizer is unique by [[lem-full-column-rank-matrix-least-squares-solution]]. After each completed sweep, increment the sweep counter. Return the current factors and model with status “budget-exhausted” after the $N_{\max}$th completed sweep. This finite-budget procedure guarantees neither convergence nor a global best CP approximation.

references.title: Tamara G. Kolda and Brett W. Bader, Tensor Decompositions and Applications, SIAM Review 51(3) (2009), §3.4
ACM 270-1, Complete Lecture Notes, Caltech, Spring 2019, Lecture 13, §4.3

items.title: Exact TT ranks and root-sum-square truncation error
items.statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$, $d\ge2$, and let $A^{\langle k\rangle}$ denote its cut-$k$ unfolding. For sequential TT-SVD, let $r_k$ be its retained bond size and $\delta_k$ its discarded singular-value tail at cut $k$. For rounding, let the input TT represent $A$ and use the same notation for the output bond sizes and recorded tails. Then both procedures satisfy
$$ \|A-\widehat A\|_F^2\le\sum_{k=1}^{d-1}\delta_k^2. $$
If no positive singular value is discarded, the output is exactly $A$. In full-rank TT-SVD, $r_k=\operatorname{rank}(A^{\langle k\rangle})$ for every cut, and these are the minimal possible TT bond sizes among exact representations.

references.title: Ivan V. Oseledets, Tensor-Train Decomposition, SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 33(5) (2011), §§2–3
Mi-Song Dupuy, Tensor trains for high-dimensional problems, full lecture notes, Chapter 1, §§1.2.1–1.2.5 (2026)

items.title: HOSVD quasioptimality for multilinear rank
items.statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$ and let $\widehat A$ be the truncated HOSVD with mode-rank caps $r_1,\ldots,r_d$. Then
$$ \|A-\widehat A\|_F \le \sqrt d\inf_{B\in\mathcal T_r}\|A-B\|_F, $$
where $\mathcal T_r$ is the set of tensors whose $k$th unfolding has rank at most $r_k$.

references.title: Lieven De Lathauwer, Bart De Moor, and Joos Vandewalle, A Multilinear Singular Value Decomposition, SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 21(4) (2000), §5, Property 10
Tamara G. Kolda and Brett W. Bader, Tensor Decompositions and Applications, SIAM Review 51(3) (2009), §4.2

items.title: Exact CP-ALS block updates do not increase the objective
items.statement: During budgeted CP-ALS, each successful exact block update does not increase the squared Frobenius residual. A rank-deficient-design halt leaves the factor matrices unchanged, so it leaves the objective unchanged. Consequently, the objective is nonincreasing over every sequence of completed exact block updates.

references.title: ACM 270-1, Complete Lecture Notes, Caltech, Spring 2019, Lecture 13, §4.3
Tamara G. Kolda and Brett W. Bader, Tensor Decompositions and Applications, SIAM Review 51(3) (2009), §3.4

title: Tensor train compression and truncation error — Examples

items.title: A best rank-two CP approximation need not exist
items.statement: Every finite tensor has a best Frobenius approximation among tensors of CP rank at most two.

references.title: Tamara G. Kolda and Brett W. Bader, Tensor Decompositions and Applications, SIAM Review 51(3) (2009), §3.3
Mi-Song Dupuy, Tensor trains for high-dimensional problems, full lecture notes, Chapter 1, §1.2.3 (2026)

items.title: A separable grid tensor has TT rank one
items.statement:
For nonzero vectors $u^{(k)}\in\mathbb R^{n_k}$, consider the separable grid tensor
$$ A=u^{(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes u^{(d)}. $$

references.title: Ivan V. Oseledets, Tensor-Train Decomposition, SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 33(5) (2011), §2
Mi-Song Dupuy, Tensor trains for high-dimensional problems, full lecture notes, Chapter 1, Example 1.2.3 (2026)

items.title: Two TT truncations realize the root-sum-square bound
items.statement: Let $A\in\mathbb R^{2\times2\times2}$ have nonzero entries $A_{111}=3$, $A_{122}=1$, and $A_{212}=2$, with all other entries zero. Apply sequential TT-SVD with rank cap one at both cuts.

references.title: Ivan V. Oseledets, Tensor-Train Decomposition, SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 33(5) (2011), §2, Theorem 2.2
Mi-Song Dupuy, Tensor trains for high-dimensional problems, full lecture notes, Chapter 1, §1.2.4 (2026)

items.title: A diagonal tensor has large minimal TT ranks
items.statement:
For integers $d\ge3$ and $n\ge2$, let
$$ A=\sum_{j=1}^{n}e_j^{(1)}\otimes e_j^{(2)}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_j^{(d)} \in\mathbb R^{n\times\cdots\times n}. $$
